title: the-one-inference-door-carries-a-tool-using-conversation
intention: inference_domain learns to carry a TOOL-USING CONVERSATION — a toolset, an assistant turn whose content is empty because its tool_calls are the content, and a tool-result turn — all the way through the canonical key to the host and back. This is CONTENT of an inference request, not a wire format: the door keeps exactly ONE inbound contract (the bus verb), and the OpenAI/OpenRouter envelope an agent harness speaks is somebody else's job.
why: Law 6 (the sole path to the inference host — a third-party agent configured to dial a provider directly IS a second door, and the only way to close it is to offer a door it already knows how to speak to); Law 3 (metering is complete only because there is no uninstrumented path — a harness outside the door is inference this system cannot measure); Telos 1 (demonstrate inference compilation — a second heavy consumer is the first real test of the yield); Law 7 (the trail records what the call did).
how: Three changes inside inference_domain, composing domain.resolve() and adding no listener, no port and no second connection. (1) host.ollama_resolver's chat branch carries a `tools` key into the /api/chat payload — measured absent, grep -c tools host.py returns 0. (2) host.validated_messages (host.py:184) GROWS A SECOND CHECKABLE SHAPE for agent turns rather than exempting them — the 2026-09-11 gate-health ruling: 'the answer is a second checkable shape, never an exemption'. (3) the zero-horizon lane for agent retries, which needs NO change to domain.py: _valid() at domain.py:252 already treats a past horizon as expired and domain.py:413 stores whatever horizon the resolver returns, so an agent resolver returning a past horizon gets a fresh sample through the charter's own clause (2) rather than around clause (1).
falsifier: DONE when (a) domain.resolve() carries a request with a `tools` list and agent-shaped turns (an assistant turn with empty content and present tool_calls, and a tool-result turn) to hex.local and back; (b) the toolset participates in the canonical digest, so the same turns under a different toolset are a different question; (c) the SECOND turn of a tool-using conversation succeeds under the proof (the one-shot green is the hollow one — the inbound argument-shape failure appears only on turn two); (d) every call lands both a row in inference_calls and an emission line in ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/, matched by canonical digest; and (e) a byte-identical retry inside an agent loop returns a FRESH sample rather than the stored one. WRONG INTENT if serving an agent turn requires EXEMPTING it from the turn-shape gate rather than growing a second checkable shape (that breaches the gate-health ruling and means the gate is in the wrong place), or if agent traffic has to be exempted from metering to be usable at all — an exemption there would mean the door cannot serve the consumer it was built for.
traces_to: Law 6 (the sole path to the inference host — a third-party agent configured to dial a provider directly IS a second door, and the only way to close it is to offer a door it already knows how to speak to); Law 3 (metering is complete only because there is no uninstrumented path — a harness outside the door is inference this system cannot measure); Telos 1 (demonstrate inference compilation — a second heavy consumer is the first real test of the yield); Law 7 (the trail records what the call did).

watchme.trigger: every inference_calls row whose canonical text carries a `tools` list — that is, every call that asked the door to carry a toolset. CAST AS 'the OpenAI-shaped door' and RESTATED 2026-09-11 at the build, because Akien's mid-voyage rescope (see `rescoped`) moved the OpenAI envelope out of this device entirely and into cairn/machines/openai_wire, held by hermes_shim. The door this probe watches is the one that survived the rescope: the bus verb carrying a toolset. A trigger naming a door that no longer lands here would never fire.
watchme.enough: when 50 toolset-carrying calls have landed AND none of them was served from cache — at that point the byte-identical-retry rate is measured rather than assumed, and the zero-horizon lane is either earning its keep or demonstrably unnecessary. The number is the ticket's, and cairn/devices/inference_domain/probes/an_agent_retry_gets_a_fresh_sample.py reads it as _ENOUGH = 50; it first carried 20 and was raised to match this spec at the build rather than the spec lowered to match it.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier clause (c): a byte-identical retry returns a FRESH sample, not the stored one
watchme.nexus: the inference_domain meter — the same store the yield report reads, so the watch costs no new table
watchme.consumer: CC, and Akien through the operator inbox if the rate says the lane was the wrong shape

cast_checks.assumption_check: ONE LOAD-BEARING ASSUMPTION IS STILL UNSTATED AND IT IS NAMED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: that a third-party harness accepts an arbitrary base_url for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Measured so far is only that hermes-agent supports OpenAI, OpenRouter, Anthropic and local providers and switches with `hermes model`. The build's FIRST act is to check that config surface, because if it is absent the seam is still right and its first consumer is not hermes. A second assumption, weaker: that OpenAI chat-completions shape maps onto the domain request without loss — roles and multi-turn message arrays have no counterpart in a single canonical prompt string, so the translation is where loss would hide.
cast_checks.missing_check: Yes, one point was asserted wrapped and is not. The intent says 'a zero-horizon lane for interactive agent traffic' as though the lane's SELECTOR were settled; it is not. What distinguishes agent traffic from any other caller — an explicit request field, a domain vertical row in stacks/domains.json, or the OpenAI door itself always requesting horizon zero — is undecided. My read, recorded so the builder is not left guessing: the door requests it, because the door is the thing that knows its callers are agents, and a request field would let any caller opt out of compilation which is the whole thesis. Not ratified.
cast_checks.falsifier_check: The intent's falsifier stands and is checkable at three named instruments: (a) an unmodified harness completes a multi-turn session; (b) every call lands BOTH an inference_calls row and an emission line in ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/, joined by canonical digest — this is the exact agreement tooth an_inference_call_logs_that_it_started already implements, so the instrument exists; (c) a byte-identical retry returns a fresh sample. HORIZON: the first real multi-turn agent session. Wrong-intent tell: the adapter needing its own host connection, which import_sieve would red at proof time without anyone having to notice.
cast_checks.collision_check: Checked the compile-once thesis (Telos 1) and it is a DISTINCTION, not a collision. The why of each side: compile-once exists so a SETTLED answer is not re-bought; an agent's retry is by definition asking for an UNSETTLED one. They are not exclusive, and the store already carries a per-answer horizon, so zero is a legal value rather than a carve-out. Also checked Law 6 sole-path: composing domain.resolve() rather than opening a socket means this ADDS no door, and import_sieve enforces that at proof and build time. Recorded distinction: inference_domain has anticipated a second protocol OUTBOUND (the gemini residue); this is the first inbound one.
cast_checks.builder_check: Wearing the cheapest-builder hat, these are answered so nobody infers them at build time. (1) WHERE: a machine under cairn/devices/inference_domain/machines/, not a new device and not a tool — it is glue over an existing primitive. (2) IT OPENS NO SOCKET: it calls domain.resolve(); if a builder reaches for httpx or requests, that is the wrong turn and import_sieve will say so. (3) WHAT SERVES IT: RULED AND CLOSED 2026-09-11 — the door opens its OWN service port and does not route to web_server. Akien: 'the web server rule was because during theigors, you were creating seperate web servers on port after port for each device. akien hereby allows the exception because this is not the User Interface web server, this is a service port.' The one-web-server rule governs the USER INTERFACE, not sockets: a UI surface faces a person and arrives as a declared pane; a service port faces a machine. The test is who is on the other end. This port exists because a third-party harness can only be configured with a base_url — a measured constraint of the consumer, not a builder convenience. It may NOT serve HTML to a human at that port; that would be the TheIgors failure exactly. Ruling: CairnCommons/decisions/2026-09-11-the-one-web-server-rule-governs-the-ui-not-service-ports.json. WAS: undecided and it matters — an HTTP listener is needed for a base_url to point at, and this system's standing rule is one web server with surfaces in the shim, never a device with its own server. THIS IS THE ONE QUESTION A BUILDER CANNOT ANSWER ALONE and it routes to web_server's owner, not to a fresh listener. (4) TRANSLATION LOSS: OpenAI sends a messages array with roles; the domain canonicalizes a request. The mapping must be deterministic and total, because canonicalization is what the cache keys on — two different message arrays flattening to one canonical string would serve one agent another agent's answer. (5) SHAPE OF THE ANSWER BACK: OpenAI's response envelope carries usage counters, and the domain already returns real cost and provenance additively, so the counters are available rather than fabricated. Do not invent them.

challenge_at_birth.better_approach: Two smaller ways, both looked at and both rejected on measurement. (a) Make the agent speak ollama instead — that requires editing the agent, which is precisely the cost this whole direction exists to avoid (922MB .git, upstream at PR #107,000, a permanent merge burden). (b) Stand a translating proxy up OUTSIDE inference_domain — rejected because it would be a SECOND thing that dials a host, which is the exact breach Law 6 and import_sieve exist to prevent. Inside the domain is not the elaborate option, it is the only one that does not open a door.
challenge_at_birth.prior_art: Consulted the compiled model after poking recompile_gate.sh: grep over CairnCommons/intentions-congruency-lab for openai / wire format / base_url returned ZERO. Nearest standing art is inference_domain's own filed residue that 'the gemini transport does not exist yet' — a second protocol on the OUTBOUND side, already anticipated. This is the same idea turned around to face INBOUND, which is a distinction to record rather than a collision.
challenge_at_birth.hidden_assumption: That hermes-agent — and harnesses generally — accept an arbitrary base_url for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. UNVERIFIED. What is measured is only that it supports OpenAI, OpenRouter, Anthropic and local providers and switches with `hermes model`. If an arbitrary base_url is not reachable through its config, this intent's value falls back to whatever other harnesses allow, and the seam is still right but its first consumer is not hermes.
challenge_at_birth.real_collision: None terminal. The nearest is the compile-once thesis itself (Telos 1): a lane that must return a fresh sample on identical bytes LOOKS like an exemption from compilation. It is not — it is a HORIZON OF ZERO, and a per-answer horizon is already a field the store carries. The why of each side agrees: compile-once exists so a settled answer is not re-bought, and an agent's retry is by definition asking for an UNsettled one. Distinction recorded.

TWO_TRANSLATIONS_THE_DOOR_OWES.outbound: ollama returns tool calls as {'function': {'name', 'arguments': <object>}}; OpenAI clients need an 'id', a 'type': 'function', and arguments as a JSON STRING.
TWO_TRANSLATIONS_THE_DOOR_OWES.inbound: THE ONE THAT BIT. OpenAI echoes those arguments back as a JSON STRING in the assistant turn; ollama /api/chat wants an OBJECT and refuses the string with HTTP 400 "Value looks like object, but can't find closing '}' symbol". Measured against hex.local qwen3-coder:30b on the SECOND turn of a tool-using conversation — turn one passed, so a one-shot test would have read green. A tooth for this belongs in the proof.

measured_before_build.validated_messages_refuses_agent_turns: cairn/devices/inference_domain/host.py:184 requires every turn to carry a non-empty string 'role' AND 'content'. An agent's assistant turn carries tool_calls with content '' and its tool-result turn carries a tool_call_id; both are legal OpenAI and both are refused today. The check is right for the chat verb and wrong for the agent verb — this is a second checkable shape, not an exemption (per the 2026-09-11 gate-health ruling).

measured_before_build.tools_belong_in_the_cache_key: The spike puts `tools` into the request dict domain.resolve canonicalizes, because the same turns under a different toolset are a different question. Confirm this at build — it is my read, not a ruling.

rescoped.by: Akien, mid-voyage, before any code was written
his_words: i approved the buildout of a openrouter interface for hermes to talk to for our inference proxy. what would that look like? enough shim so he can talk to his shim, which will route the call to the inference proxy. not an openrouter port on the inference proxy. the shims handle all the interfacing with the outside world. it's what allows us to integrate a device. adding a port on the inference proxy, as sensible as that is, and it really is, the architecture wants to force everything to be similar specifically because fewer things to know as you or i switch between pieces. extra work to make it all the same to be sure. but all the same means less cogniting on which path is right.
and if you build it as it's own machine, then anybody can include it
rescoped.what_was_wrong: The cast put an OpenAI-shaped LISTENER on inference_domain — a second inbound wire format on the device. That gives the device two doors, so a mind arriving cold at inference_domain has to work out which door a call came through before anything else makes sense. The shim pattern already standing at cairn/devices/aider_shim keeps ALL foreignness at the edge: holder.py holds the foreign tool's surfaces, fence.py bounds what it may ask, translate.py speaks both tongues, and no other device has ever heard of aider. CC read 'openrouter interface' as an OUTBOUND provider (Cairn dialing openrouter.ai) and filed it in constrain's `out` bounds; it is INBOUND — the face a shim presents to hermes.

the_split.548dd13fb4db (this ticket): inference_domain carries a tool-using conversation. No wire format, no listener, no port. The layer below — built and proved first.
the_split.NEW: cairn/machines/openai_wire: a MACHINE, not a device and nobody's property: translate.py (pure OpenAI body <-> canonical request, answer <-> chat-completions envelope, tool_calls arguments JSON-string <-> object both ways) and serve.py (an HTTP handler composed with an INJECTED resolve callable — opens no socket at import, dials no host). Injection is what makes 'anybody can include it' true rather than aspirational, and it is the shape domain.resolve(request, *, resolver=...) already stands on.
the_split.cb97524c0e8e: hermes_shim holds openai_wire, injects the bus call to inference_domain, and owns the port choice, the fence, and ~/.hermes/config.yaml.

rescoped.cc_read_not_ruled: The toolset belongs IN the canonical cache key — the same turns under a different toolset are a different question, and a cache that ignored `tools` would serve an answer computed under capabilities the caller no longer has. Carried into the falsifier so it is checkable and visible rather than buried; Akien has not ruled it and can flip it.
rescoped.gap_noticed: There is no write door for an ALREADY-CAST ticket. skills/sorted/door.py casts, and cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit moves the cursor, but a scope correction like this one is a hand edit of the JSON with nothing judging it. Not this voyage's work; recorded here so it is a measurement rather than a habit.
